description: ASHE publishes energy benchmarks for US hospitals from data collected through its Energy to Care programme from hundreds of participating general medical and surgical hospitals. The 'Energy Use Benchmarking Deep Dive for U.S. Hospitals', aimed at facility managers, engineers, designers and academics, covers demographics and methods, changes in consumption since 2018, year-to-year and weather-related variation, median source energy use intensity by climate zone for 2023, typical carbon per square foot, natural gas use, peak electrical demand, energy and water costs and their changes from 2022 to 2023; a companion 'Energy Benchmarking for US Hospitals' report gives authorities having jurisdiction regional benchmarks from 2018 to 2022 data to help set energy use intensity targets. Coverage: US hospitals in the programme. Access: digital reports sold by ASHE (74 US dollars for members, 94 for non-members when read). Licence: proprietary. Caveats: aggregated benchmarks from a voluntary sample, not facility-level data. Simulation uses: reference energy intensities and peak demand for hospital energy models, emergency power sizing and decarbonisation scenarios. Related records: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the NHS hospital estates statistics.
